title: Hox/Wnt interact to pattern the primary body axis of an anthozoan cnidarian prior to gastrulation
protocol: Collect embryos or small polyps by swirling them around in the dish and pipetting off garbage, minimizing water.
Add 1 mL Trizol to each tube of embryos; vortex lightly if needed.
Spin down heavy phase lock tubes at 4°C.
Transfer phenol containing dissolved embryos into heavy phase lock tubes.
Add 200 μL chloroform to each tube and shake well for 15 seconds.
Incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Spin down at max speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Spin down new, empty phase lock tubes for 1 minute; transfer aqueous phase to the new phase lock tubes.
Add 600 μL phenol-chloroform-isoamyl-alcohol to each tube and shake for 15 seconds.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Spin down at max speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer aqueous phase to new, clean 1.5 mL tubes using a barrier tip carefully.
Add 1 μl glycogen.
Add 500 μl isopropanol, shake, and incubate at room temperature for 10-20 minutes.
Spin at max speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Remove liquid being careful to avoid pellet; spin again for 10 seconds and remove more liquid.
Add ~890 μl RNase-free 70% EtOH stored at -20°C.
Vortex the mixture.
Remove liquid, avoiding the pellet.
Spin down briefly and remove liquid again.
Repeat adding ~890 μl RNase-free 70% EtOH and vortexing.
Remove liquid after addition of ethanol, avoiding the pellet.
Spin down briefly and remove liquid again.
Let the pellet dry thoroughly.
Add 10 μl RNase free water to the dried pellet.
Mix 0.5 mL Trizol with small polyps and homogenize.
Add another 0.5 mL Trizol to the mixture.
Spin down heavy phase lock tubes at 4°C.
Transfer phenol containing dissolved embryos into the heavy phase lock tubes.
Add 200 μL chloroform to each tube and shake for 15 seconds.
Incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Spin down at maximum speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Spin down new, empty phase lock tubes for 1 minute.
Transfer the aqueous phase to the new phase lock tubes.
Add 600 μL phenol-chloroform-isoamyl-alcohol to each tube and shake for 15 seconds.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Spin down at maximum speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the aqueous phase to new, clean 1.5 mL tubes using a barrier tip carefully.
Add 1 μL glycogen to each tube.
Add 500 μL isopropanol, shake and incubate at room temperature for 10-20 minutes.
Spin down at maximum speed for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the liquid being careful not to disturb the pellet; spin again briefly and remove more liquid.
Add ~890 μL RNase-free 70% EtOH stored at -20°C, vortex thoroughly.
Remove the liquid avoiding the pellet; spin down briefly and remove liquid again.
Repeat steps for adding 890 μL RNase-free 70% EtOh and removing the liquid carefully to ensure all is removed.
Let the pellet dry thoroughly.
Add 10 μL RNase free water to rehydrate the dried pellet.
Amplify the probe sequence from cDNA using selected primers.

Mix 5 μl of 10x reaction buffer, 0.5 μl of dNTPs (10 mM), 0.5 μl of Taq polymerase, 41 μl of nuclease-free water, 1.0 μl of forward primer (10 μM), 1.0 μl of reverse primer (10 μM), and 1.0 μl of template cDNA.
Run the PCR product on a 1% agarose gel.
Excise the DNA fragment from the agarose gel with a clean, sharp scalpel.
Weigh the gel slice in a colorless tube.
Add 400 μl of Buffer QG to 1 volume of gel (or just add 400 μl).
Incubate at 50°C for 10 min until the gel slice has completely dissolved.
Vortex the tube every 2–3 min during incubation to help dissolve the gel.
After complete dissolution, check that the color of the mixture is yellow.
Add 10 μl 3 M sodium acetate, pH 5.0, to the mixture and mix.
Mix 1 gel volume of isopropanol with the sample.
Place a MinElute spin column in a provided 2 ml collection tube.
Apply the sample to the MinElute column and centrifuge for 1 minute.
Discard flow-through and place the MinElute column back into the same collection tube.
Add 500 μl Buffer QG to the MinElute column and centrifuge for 1 minute.
Discard flow-through and place the MinElute column back into the same collection tube.
Add 750 μl Buffer PE to the MinElute column and centrifuge for 1 minute.
Discard flow-through and place the MinElute column back into the same collection tube.
Centrifuge the column in a 2 ml collection tube for 1 minute.
Place each MinElute column into a clean 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Add 10 μl water to the center of the MinElute membrane to elute DNA.
Briefly centrifuge the pGEM®-T or pGEM®-T Easy Vector and Control Insert DNA tubes to collect contents.
Set up ligation reactions as described in protocol.
Mix the reactions by pipetting.
Incubate the reactions for 1 hour at room temperature.
Alternatively, if maximum number of transformants is required, incubate the reactions overnight at 16°C.
Add 2 μl of each ligation to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Remove tubes of frozen JM109 High Efficiency Competent Cells from freezer and place on ice.
Thaw cells in an ice bath until just thawed (about 5 minutes).
Gently flick the tube to mix the cells.
Transfer 50 μl of cells into each prepared tube.
Mix gently and place tubes on ice for 20 minutes.
Heat-shock the cells for 45–50 seconds at exactly 42°C in a water bath without shaking.
Return the tubes immediately to ice for 2 minutes.
Add 460 μl room-temperature LB medium to tubes containing ligation reaction-transformed cells.
Add 900 μl room-temperature LB medium to the tube with uncut plasmid-transformed cells.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C with shaking (~150 rpm) for 1.5 hours.
Plate 100 μl of each transformation culture onto LB/ampicillin plates.
Centrifuge cells at 1,000 × g for 10 minutes if a higher number of colonies is desired.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 200 μl of LB medium.
Plate 100 μl on two plates if more colonies are needed.
Incubate the plates overnight (16–24 hours) at 37°C.
Perform colony PCR to determine which colonies contain PCR fragment.
Add 2.5 μl of 10x reaction buffer to the PCR solution.
Add 0.25 μl of dNTPs (10 mM) to the PCR solution.
Add 0.5 μl of Taq polymerase to the PCR solution.
Add 19.75 μl of nuclease-free water to the PCR solution.
Add 1.0 μl of Sp6 primer (10 μM) to the PCR solution.
Add 1.0 μl of T7 primer (10 μM) to the PCR solution.
Mix all components thoroughly in the PCR solution.
Amplify for 40 cycles.
Pour 3 ml LB into a glass culture tube.
Touch a pipette tip to the chosen colony, then drop it into the LB in the tube.
Incubate overnight with shaking.
Chill the Complete Lysis Solution on ice.
Pellet 1.5 ml of fresh bacterial culture at maximum speed for 1 minute in the provided 2 ml Culture Tube.
Remove medium by decanting, taking care not to disturb bacterial pellet.
Add 400 μl of ICE-COLD Complete Lysis Solution.
Mix thoroughly by constant vortexing at the highest setting for a full 30 seconds.
Incubate the lysate at room temperature for 3 minutes.
Transfer the lysate to a Spin Column Assembly by decanting or pipetting.
Centrifuge the Spin Column Assembly for 30–60 seconds at maximum speed.
Add 400 μl of DILUTED Wash Buffer to the Spin Column Assembly.
Centrifuge the Spin Column Assembly for 30–60 seconds at maximum speed.
Remove the Spin Column from the centrifuge and decant the filtrate from the Waste Tube.
Place the Spin Column back into the Waste Tube and return it to the centrifuge.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 1 minute to dry the Spin Column.
Transfer the Spin Column into a Collection Tube.
Add 50 μl of Elution Buffer directly to the center of the Spin Column membrane and cap the Collection Tube over the Spin Column.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 30 – 60 seconds.
Remove and discard the Spin Column.
The eluted DNA can be used immediately for downstream applications or stored at -20°C.
